Amazon.Level decided by: nothing — always on the member; the parent row carries zero populated fields (two observations).
Amazon.Field / mechanism: admission control: “Child ASINs with different non-varying attribute values cannot be grouped into a single variation family.”
Amazon.Example: ● parent and three children byte-identical on title stem, description, bullet-point1, search-terms, item-type, target-audience, main-image-url — replicated (Flat.File.Home.xls)

Shopify.Level decided by: the definition: MetafieldDefinition.ownerType: MetafieldOwnerType! — one value per definition (PRODUCT or PRODUCTVARIANT, among 26).
Shopify.Field / mechanism: two separate definitions for two levels; built-ins fixed (variant: price, sku, barcode, selectedOptions, media; product: title, description, category, vendor, options).
Shopify.Read-time fallback?: no (images: variant media or product media, chosen by the merchant).

Google.Level decided by: nothing — no family object on the write side; every row is self-describing.
Google.Example: ● "itemGroupId": "cp0905-grp-flavor", "itemGroupTitle": "cp0905 u3 flavor group" on each member

eBay.Level decided by: ambiguous — slots at both levels (InventoryItemGroup.aspects, InventoryItem.product.aspects) and a flag on the definition, aspectApplicableTo ∈ {ITEM, PRODUCT} — but the flag is about eBay's catalogue product vs a seller instance, not group vs item.

Walmart.Level decided by: nothing — no container; “shared by repetition, not reference”.
Walmart.Example: ● "productName": "Colgate Crest Toothpaste" repeated on both members of group 001960968586AX6

Shopee.Level decided by: the API's structure — the item carries attribute_list; the model has no attribute slot.
Shopee.Field / mechanism: no level field; three physical fields inherit by rule.
Shopee.Read-time fallback?: yes for weight, dimension, pre_order: “If don't set the weight of this model, will use the weight of item by default.”

Tokopedia.Field / mechanism: consumed on two objects — product_attributes[] on the product, skus[].sales_attributes[] on the SKU; physical dimensions exist at both levels (package_dimensions/package_weight vs sku_dimensions/sku_weight).

Square.Field / mechanism: an ITEM-allowed and an ITEM_VARIATION-allowed definition are separate definitions; values do not flow down; the array may carry both types.

Salesforce B2C.Level decided by: read time — one <product> complexType serves master and variant.
Salesforce B2C.Field / mechanism: “If the variant does not define an own value, the value is retrieved by fallback from variation groups (sorted by their position) or the variation master.”
Salesforce B2C.Example: ◇ master name = "Low Top Shoes", variant leaves name unset → reads the master's; sets its own description → overrides

Akeneo.Level decided by: the family variant: FamilyVariant.variant_attribute_sets[] {level, axes, attributes} assigns each attribute to exactly one level (1 or 2); common attributes stay on the product model.
Akeneo.Field / mechanism: levels are attribute-disjoint; moving an attribute keeps existing values (“the description previously filled in will be kept for all variant products, but you can change it”).
Akeneo.Read-time fallback?: no — values live at their level.

WooCommerce.Level decided by: the API's structure — container postmeta (_product_attributes, _default_attributes, terms, child ids) vs the variation's attribute_<key> rows.
WooCommerce.Read-time fallback?: yes for stock by an explicit sentinel — manage_stock = 'parent'.

commercetools.Level decided by: the definition: AttributeDefinition.level: Product | Variant (draft default Variant; immutable in the UI).
commercetools.Field / mechanism: product-level attributes must have attributeConstraint: None (being product-level is same-for-all; DuplicateAttributeValuesError otherwise); Classic model: ProductData.attributes vs ProductVariant.attributes.
commercetools.Read-time fallback?: no; Modular VariantProjection.description? is a read-only projection of the parent's.
commercetools.Example: ● "level": "Product" — “not supported by Product Projection Search” (deprecated); vendor doc examples only (U1)

Magento.Level decided by: nothing — every EAV value row is keyed (entity_id, attribute_id, store_id); parent and child each own theirs; no use_parent column.
Magento.Field / mechanism: is_global is a store scope (SCOPE_STORE=0, SCOPE_GLOBAL=1), not a level.
Magento.Example: ● catalog_product_entity_varchar {entity_id: 93 (parent), attribute_id: name, …} and a separate row for each child
